{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793142133187,"sessionID":"ses_e807c23a9ffecLzhcZkkw485d1","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_018HYsuqJaCavFueRw5WnhLf","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/floydwarshall_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition\n//   * MPI:    the NB x NB grid of TILE x TILE tiles is distributed block-cyclically\n//             over a P x Q process grid. Tile (I,J) belongs to rank (I%P, J%Q).\n//             Each rank drives one GPU (local rank modulo device count).\n//   * CUDA:   blocked Floyd-Warshall. For each block index K the pivot tile (K,K),\n//             the row/column panels (K,J)/(I,K) are processed first, then the tiles\n//             of row/column K+1 (needed by the next block) and finally all remaining\n//             tiles are relaxed with the TILE pivots of block K fused in registers.\n//             Work is pipelined: the bulk update of block K runs on a second stream\n//             while the host exchanges block K+1's pivot data over MPI.\n//   * OpenMP: host-side data-parallel loops (tile initialization, result gathering).\n//\n// Equivalence with the sequential k-outer algorithm\n//   Every tile receives the same sequence of relaxations as the original code, in\n//   ascending k order: the pivot phases inside a block replay k in order, and each\n//   tile is updated by block K only after block K-1 has been applied to it (ordered\n//   by stream/event dependencies). For every phase the pivot column and row are\n//   captured exactly as they are at the start of that phase (snapshots), so\n//   distances and path entries (strict '<' tie-breaking) are identical. Padding\n//   (n rounded up to a multiple of TILE) only holds INF rows/columns whose pivots\n//   are skipped, so they never influence real entries.\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr unsigned int INF = 1000000000;\nconstexpr unsigned int MAX_DISTANCE = 200;\n\nconstexpr int TILE = 64;           // tile edge length (pivots fused per block)\nconstexpr int TT = TILE * TILE;    // elements per tile\nconstexpr int THREADS = 256;       // 16 x 16 threads per CUDA block\nconstexpr int RPT = TILE / 16;     // elements per thread per dimension\nstatic_assert(RPT * 16 == TILE, \"TILE must be a multiple of 16\");\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                 \\\n    do {                                                                                 \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                       \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                       \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error '%s' at %s:%d: %s\\n\", cudaGetErrorString(err_),  \\\n                    __FILE__, __LINE__, #call);                                          \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                \\\n        }                                                                                \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Index calculation for flattened 2D array\ninline constexpr size_t idx2(const size_t i, const size_t j, const size_t n) noexcept {\n    return j * n + i;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Device kernels\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nenum PanelMode { PANEL_DIAG = 0, PANEL_COL = 1, PANEL_ROW = 2 };\n\n// Processes the pivot phases of block K inside one tile per CUDA block.\n//   PANEL_DIAG: tile (K,K), in place. snapOut receives\n//               diagRow[kp][y] = D(K.kp, K.y) and diagCol[kp][x] = D(K.x, K.kp)\n//               as they are at the start of phase kp (2*TT entries).\n//   PANEL_COL:  tile (I,K), I != K, local tile row blockIdx.x. piv is the diag\n//               snapshot; snapOut receives colSnap[kp][x] = D(I.x, K.kp).\n//   PANEL_ROW:  tile (K,J), J != K, local tile column blockIdx.x. piv is the diag\n//               snapshot; snapOut receives rowSnap[kp][y] = D(K.kp, J.y).\n// gStart/gStep map the block index to the global tile index (used to skip the\n// pivot tile itself).\ntemplate <int MODE>\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(THREADS)\npanelKernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ gDist, unsigned int* __restrict__ gPath,\n            const size_t blockStride, const int gStart, const int gStep, const int K,\n            const int kBase, const int kmax, const unsigned int* __restrict__ piv,\n            unsigned int* __restrict__ snapOut) {\n    if (MODE != PANEL_DIAG && gStart + static_cast<int>(blockIdx.x) * gStep == K) {\n        return;  // the pivot tile itself is handled by PANEL_DIAG\n    }\n\n    unsigned int* D = gDist + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockStride;\n    unsigned int* P = gPath + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockStride;\n    unsigned int* S = snapOut + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * 2 * TT;\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int sD[TT];   // distances, storage index yl*TILE + xl\n    __shared__ unsigned int sP[TT];   // path\n    __shared__ unsigned int pc[TILE]; // pivot column for the current phase\n    __shared__ unsigned int pr[TILE]; // pivot row for the current phase\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int tx = tid & 15;\n    const int ty = tid >> 4;\n\n    for (int t = tid; t < TT; t += THREADS) {\n        sD[t] = D[t];\n        sP[t] = P[t];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int kp = 0; kp < kmax; ++kp) {\n        __syncthreads();  // previous phase fully applied\n        if (tid < TILE) {\n            if (MODE == PANEL_DIAG) {\n                pc[tid] = sD[kp * TILE + tid];   // D(x=tid, kp)\n                pr[tid] = sD[tid * TILE + kp];   // D(kp, y=tid)\n            } else if (MODE == PANEL_COL) {\n                pc[tid] = sD[kp * TILE + tid];   // D(x=tid, kp), local column kp\n                pr[tid] = piv[kp * TILE + tid];  // diagRow[kp][y]\n            } else {\n                pr[tid] = sD[tid * TILE + kp];   // D(kp, y=tid), local row kp\n                pc[tid] = piv[TT + kp * TILE + tid];  // diagCol[kp][x]\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (tid < TILE) {\n            if (MODE == PANEL_DIAG) {\n                S[kp * TILE + tid] = pr[tid];\n                S[TT + kp * TILE + tid] = pc[tid];\n            } else if (MODE == PANEL_COL) {\n                S[kp * TILE + tid] = pc[tid];\n            } else {\n                S[kp * TILE + tid] = pr[tid];\n            }\n        }\n\n        const unsigned int kg = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kp);\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int a = 0; a < RPT; ++a) {\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int b = 0; b < RPT; ++b) {\n                const int x = tx + 16 * a;\n                const int y = ty + 16 * b;\n                const int idx = y * TILE + x;\n                const unsigned int nd = pc[x] + pr[y];\n                if (nd < sD[idx]) {\n                    sD[idx] = nd;\n                    sP[idx] = kg;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int t = tid; t < TT; t += THREADS) {\n        D[t] = sD[t];\n        P[t] = sP[t];\n    }\n}\n\n// Relaxes local tiles (I,J) with I != K and J != K using the kmax pivots of block K.\n// part == UPDATE_CRITICAL: only tiles of row K+1 or column K+1 (needed by block K+1).\n// part == UPDATE_BULK:     all remaining tiles of block K.\n// colSnap[li*TT + kp*TILE + x] = D(I.x, K.kp), rowSnap[lj*TT + kp*TILE + y] = D(K.kp, J.y).\n// Grid: (NLJ, NLI) local tiles.\nenum UpdatePart { UPDATE_CRITICAL = 0, UPDATE_BULK = 1 };\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(THREADS)\nupdateKernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ gDist, unsigned int* __restrict__ gPath,\n             const int NLJ, const int r, const int c, const int P, const int Q, const int K,\n             const int kBase, const int kmax, const int part,\n             const unsigned int* __restrict__ colSnap,\n             const unsigned int* __restrict__ rowSnap) {\n    const int lj = blockIdx.x;\n    const int li = blockIdx.y;\n    const int I = r + li * P;\n    const int J = c + lj * Q;\n    if (I == K || J == K) return;\n    const bool critical = (I == K + 1 || J == K + 1);\n    if (critical != (part == UPDATE_CRITICAL)) return;\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int sCol[TT];  // sCol[kp*TILE + x] = D(I.x, K.kp)\n    __shared__ unsigned int sRow[TT];  // sRow[kp*TILE + y] = D(K.kp, J.y)\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int tx = tid & 15;\n    const int ty = tid >> 4;\n\n    const unsigned int* cs = colSnap + static_cast<size_t>(li) * TT;\n    const unsigned int* rs = rowSnap + static_cast<size_t>(lj) * TT;\n    for (int t = tid; t < kmax * TILE; t += THREADS) {\n        sCol[t] = cs[t];\n        sRow[t] = rs[t];\n    }\n\n    const size_t base = (static_cast<size_t>(li) * NLJ + lj) * TT;\n    unsigned int* D = gDist + base;\n    unsigned int* Pa = gPath + base;\n\n    unsigned int d[RPT][RPT];\n    unsigned int p[RPT][RPT];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int a = 0; a < RPT; ++a) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int b = 0; b < RPT; ++b) {\n            const int idx = (ty + 16 * b) * TILE + (tx + 16 * a);\n            d[a][b] = D[idx];\n            p[a][b] = Pa[idx];\n        }\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int kp = 0; kp < kmax; ++kp) {\n        unsigned int cv[RPT];\n        unsigned int rv[RPT];\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int a = 0; a < RPT; ++a) cv[a] = sCol[kp * TILE + tx + 16 * a];\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int b = 0; b < RPT; ++b) rv[b] = sRow[kp * TILE + ty + 16 * b];\n\n        const unsigned int kg = static_cast<unsigned int>(kBase + kp);\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int a = 0; a < RPT; ++a) {\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int b = 0; b < RPT; ++b) {\n                const unsigned int nd = cv[a] + rv[b];\n                if (nd < d[a][b]) {\n                    d[a][b] = nd;\n                    p[a][b] = kg;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int a = 0; a < RPT; ++a) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int b = 0; b < RPT; ++b) {\n            const int idx = (ty + 16 * b) * TILE + (tx + 16 * a);\n            D[idx] = d[a][b];\n            Pa[idx] = p[a][b];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Host side\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Number of indices in [0, numTiles) congruent to `index` modulo `dim`.\nstatic inline int localCount(const int numTiles, const int index, const int dim) {\n    return numTiles > index ? (numTiles - index - 1) / dim + 1 : 0;\n}\n\nstruct Decomposition {\n    int P = 1, Q = 1;       // process grid: P process rows, Q process columns\n    int r = 0, c = 0;       // this rank's grid coordinates (rank = r*Q + c)\n    int NB = 0;             // tiles per matrix dimension\n    int NLI = 0, NLJ = 0;   // locally owned tile rows / tile columns\n    MPI_Comm rowComm = MPI_COMM_NULL;  // ranks sharing r; rank index equals c\n    MPI_Comm colComm = MPI_COMM_NULL;  // ranks sharing c; rank index equals r\n};\n\nstatic Decomposition makeDecomposition(const int rank, const int size, const size_t n) {\n    Decomposition d;\n    int dims[2] = {0, 0};\n    MPI_Dims_create(size, 2, dims);\n    d.P = dims[0];\n    d.Q = dims[1];\n    d.r = rank / d.Q;\n    d.c = rank % d.Q;\n    d.NB = static_cast<int>((n + TILE - 1) / TILE);\n    d.NLI = localCount(d.NB, d.r, d.P);\n    d.NLJ = localCount(d.NB, d.c, d.Q);\n    MPI_Comm_split(MPI_COMM_WORLD, d.r, d.c, &d.rowComm);\n    MPI_Comm_split(MPI_COMM_WORLD, d.c, d.r, &d.colComm);\n    return d;\n}\n\nstatic void selectDevice() {\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices available\\n\");\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    MPI_Comm shm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, 0, MPI_INFO_NULL, &shm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(shm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&shm);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(localRank % numDevices));\n}\n\n// Fills this rank's tiles. The random values are identical to the original\n// initializeDistanceMatrix(): rand_r (seed 42) consumed in storage order\n// (element (x,y) at index y*n + x). The path matrix equals the original\n// initializePathMatrix(), which yields path(x,y) = y.\nstatic void initializeLocalTiles(const Decomposition& d, const size_t n,\n                                 unsigned int* dist, unsigned int* path) {\n    const long long numLocal = static_cast<long long>(d.NLI) * d.NLJ;\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long long t = 0; t < numLocal; ++t) {\n        const int li = static_cast<int>(t / d.NLJ);\n        const int lj = static_cast<int>(t % d.NLJ);\n        const size_t I = static_cast<size_t>(d.r + li * d.P);\n        const size_t J = static_cast<size_t>(d.c + lj * d.Q);\n        unsigned int* D = dist + static_cast<size_t>(t) * TT;\n        unsigned int* Pa = path + static_cast<size_t>(t) * TT;\n        for (int yl = 0; yl < TILE; ++yl) {\n            for (int xl = 0; xl < TILE; ++xl) {\n                const size_t x = I * TILE + xl;\n                const size_t y = J * TILE + yl;\n                D[yl * TILE + xl] = (x == y) ? 0u : INF;  // padding stays INF\n                Pa[yl * TILE + xl] = static_cast<unsigned int>(y);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    const unsigned int rangeMin = 1;\n    const unsigned int rangeMax = MAX_DISTANCE;\n    const double range = static_cast<double>(rangeMax - rangeMin) + 1.0;\n\n    // Serial by necessity: the rand_r stream must be consumed in storage order.\n    for (size_t y = 0; y < n; ++y) {\n        const int J = static_cast<int>(y / TILE);\n        const int yl = static_cast<int>(y % TILE);\n        const bool colOwned = (J % d.Q) == d.c;\n        const int lj = J / d.Q;\n        for (size_t x = 0; x < n; ++x) {\n            const unsigned int value =\n                rangeMin + (unsigned int)(range * rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX);\n            const int I = static_cast<int>(x / TILE);\n            if (colOwned && (I % d.P) == d.r) {\n                const int li = I / d.P;\n                const size_t t = static_cast<size_t>(li) * d.NLJ + lj;\n                dist[t * TT + yl * TILE + static_cast<int>(x % TILE)] = (x == y) ? 0u : value;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Device and host resources for the pipelined block loop.\nstruct Pipeline {\n    cudaStream_t sMain = nullptr;  // pivot tile, panels, snapshot exchange, tiles of row/col K+1\n    cudaStream_t sBulk = nullptr;  // all remaining tiles\n    cudaEvent_t evBulk[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};      // bulk of block K finished\n    cudaEvent_t evSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};      // device snapshots of block K ready\n    cudaEvent_t evHostFree[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};  // host staging of block K no longer in use\n\n    unsigned int* dDiagSnap = nullptr;   // 2*TT, pivot tile snapshot (main stream only)\n    unsigned int* dColSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};  // NLI*TT, per block parity\n    unsigned int* dRowSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};  // NLJ*TT, per block parity\n\n    unsigned int* hDiagSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};\n    unsigned int* hColSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};\n    unsigned int* hRowSnap[2] = {nullptr, nullptr};\n};\n\n// Runs the blocked Floyd-Warshall over all tiles. The rank's tiles stay on the device;\n// only pivot snapshots travel through pinned host staging buffers.\nstatic void runBlockedFloydWarshall(const Decomposition& d, const size_t n,\n                                    unsigned int* dDist, unsigned int* dPath, Pipeline& pl) {\n    const size_t colElems = static_cast<size_t>(d.NLI) * TT;\n    const size_t rowElems = static_cast<size_t>(d.NLJ) * TT;\n    const size_t diagBytes = 2 * TT * sizeof(unsigned int);\n\n    for (int K = 0; K < d.NB; ++K) {\n        const int b = K & 1;\n        const int kBase = K * TILE;\n        const int kmax = static_cast<int>(std::min<size_t>(TILE, n - static_cast<size_t>(kBase)));\n        const bool ownsRow = (K % d.P) == d.r;  // this rank holds tile row K\n        const bool ownsCol = (K % d.Q) == d.c;  // this rank holds tile column K\n        const bool ownsDiag = ownsRow && ownsCol;\n        const int diagRoot = (K % d.P) * d.Q + (K % d.Q);\n\n        // Host staging of parity b was last used by block K-2; wait until its copies finished.\n        if (K >= 2) CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventSynchronize(pl.evHostFree[b]));\n\n        // 1. Pivot tile (K,K) on the owner; broadcast its row/column snapshots.\n        if (ownsDiag) {\n            const size_t off = (static_cast<size_t>(K / d.P) * d.NLJ + (K / d.Q)) * TT;\n            panelKernel<PANEL_DIAG><<<1, THREADS, 0, pl.sMain>>>(\n                dDist + off, dPath + off, 0, 0, 1, K, kBase, kmax, nullptr, pl.dDiagSnap);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.hDiagSnap[b], pl.dDiagSnap, diagBytes,\n                                       cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, pl.sMain));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(pl.sMain));\n        }\n        MPI_Bcast(pl.hDiagSnap[b], 2 * TT, MPI_UNSIGNED, diagRoot, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n        if (!ownsDiag) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.dDiagSnap, pl.hDiagSnap[b], diagBytes,\n                                       cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, pl.sMain));\n        }\n\n        // 2. Column panel (I,K) and row panel (K,J) on their owners.\n        if (ownsCol && d.NLI > 0) {\n            panelKernel<PANEL_COL><<<d.NLI, THREADS, 0, pl.sMain>>>(\n                dDist + static_cast<size_t>(K / d.Q) * TT, dPath + static_cast<size_t>(K / d.Q) * TT,\n                static_cast<size_t>(d.NLJ) * TT, d.r, d.P, K, kBase, kmax, pl.dDiagSnap,\n                pl.dColSnap[b]);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n        if (ownsRow && d.NLJ > 0) {\n            const size_t off = static_cast<size_t>(K / d.P) * d.NLJ * TT;\n            panelKernel<PANEL_ROW><<<d.NLJ, THREADS, 0, pl.sMain>>>(\n                dDist + off, dPath + off, TT, d.c, d.Q, K, kBase, kmax, pl.dDiagSnap,\n                pl.dRowSnap[b]);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n\n        // 3. Exchange panel snapshots: column panels along process rows,\n        //    row panels along process columns.\n        if (ownsCol && colElems > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.hColSnap[b], pl.dColSnap[b],\n                                       colElems * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost,\n                                       pl.sMain));\n        }\n        if (ownsRow && rowElems > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.hRowSnap[b], pl.dRowSnap[b],\n                                       rowElems * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost,\n                                       pl.sMain));\n        }\n        if ((ownsCol && colElems > 0) || (ownsRow && rowElems > 0)) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(pl.sMain));\n        }\n        if (colElems > 0) {\n            MPI_Bcast(pl.hColSnap[b], static_cast<int>(colElems), MPI_UNSIGNED, K % d.Q, d.rowComm);\n        }\n        if (rowElems > 0) {\n            MPI_Bcast(pl.hRowSnap[b], static_cast<int>(rowElems), MPI_UNSIGNED, K % d.P, d.colComm);\n        }\n        if (!ownsCol && colElems > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.dColSnap[b], pl.hColSnap[b],\n                                       colElems * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice,\n                                       pl.sMain));\n        }\n        if (!ownsRow && rowElems > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(pl.dRowSnap[b], pl.hRowSnap[b],\n                                       rowElems * sizeof(unsigned int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice,\n                                       pl.sMain));\n        }\n        // Host staging of parity b can be reused once these copies have completed.\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventRecord(pl.evHostFree[b], pl.sMain));\n\n        // Snapshots of block K are ready on the device; bulk work of block K may start\n        // once the bulk work of block K-1 has finished (same stream, in order).\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventRecord(pl.evSnap[b], pl.sMain));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(pl.sBulk, pl.evSnap[b], 0));\n\n        // 4. Bulk tiles of block K, concurrent with the host-side work of later blocks.\n        if (d.NLI > 0 && d.NLJ > 0) {\n            updateKernel<<<dim3(d.NLJ, d.NLI), THREADS, 0, pl.sBulk>>>(\n                dDist, dPath, d.NLJ, d.r, d.c, d.P, d.Q, K, kBase, kmax, UPDATE_BULK,\n                pl.dColSnap[b], pl.dRowSnap[b]);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventRecord(pl.evBulk[b], pl.sBulk));\n\n        // 5. Tiles of row/column K+1 (the next pivot block) on the main stream. They\n        //    depend on block K-1 having been applied to them, which the bulk stream\n        //    provides through evBulk[K-1].\n        if (K >= 1) CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(pl.sMain, pl.evBulk[b ^ 1], 0));\n        if (d.NLI > 0 && d.NLJ > 0) {\n            updateKernel<<<dim3(d.NLJ, d.NLI), THREADS, 0, pl.sMain>>>(\n                dDist, dPath, d.NLJ, d.r, d.c, d.P, d.Q, K, kBase, kmax, UPDATE_CRITICAL,\n                pl.dColSnap[b], pl.dRowSnap[b]);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        }\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n}\n\n// Places the tiles of rank (rr,cc) (packed as [tile][yl][xl]) into the full\n// matrix stored in the original layout (element (x,y) at y*n + x).\nstatic void scatterTiles(const unsigned int* src, const int rr, const int cc, const Decomposition& d,\n                         const size_t n, std::vector<unsigned int>& out) {\n    const int NLI = localCount(d.NB, rr, d.P);\n    const int NLJ = localCount(d.NB, cc, d.Q);\n    const long long numLocal = static_cast<long long>(NLI) * NLJ;\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (long long t = 0; t < numLocal; ++t) {\n        const int li = static_cast<int>(t / NLJ);\n        const int lj = static_cast<int>(t % NLJ);\n        const size_t I = static_cast<size_t>(rr + li * d.P);\n        const size_t J = static_cast<size_t>(cc + lj * d.Q);\n        const unsigned int* S = src + static_cast<size_t>(t) * TT;\n        for (int yl = 0; yl < TILE; ++yl) {\n            const size_t y = J * TILE + yl;\n            if (y >= n) break;\n            for (int xl = 0; xl < TILE; ++xl) {\n                const size_t x = I * TILE + xl;\n                if (x >= n) break;\n                out[y * n + x] = S[yl * TILE + xl];\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Gathers the distance matrix onto rank 0 (only needed for -r / -v).\nstatic void gatherDistances(const Decomposition& d, const int rank, const int size, const size_t n,\n                            const unsigned int* hLocal, std::vector<unsigned int>& full) {\n    const size_t localElems = static_cast<size_t>(d.NLI) * d.NLJ * TT;\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        full.assign(n * n, 0u);\n        scatterTiles(hLocal, 0, 0, d, n, full);\n        std::vector<unsigned int> buf;\n        for (int rr = 1; Diagonal should be zero\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numNodes; ++i) {\n        if (dist[idx2(i, i, numNodes)] != 0) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: diagonal element [%zu,%zu] is not zero\\n\", i, i);\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // 2. {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < std::min(numNodes, static_cast<size_t>(10)); ++j) {\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < numNodes; ++k) {\n                const unsigned int distIJ = dist[idx2(j, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distIK = dist[idx2(k, i, numNodes)];\n                const unsigned int distKJ = dist[idx2(j, k, numNodes)];\n\n                // Check for overflow before addition\n                if (distIK < INF && distKJ < INF) {\n                    if (distIK + distKJ < distIJ) {\n                        printf(\"Validation failed: triangle inequality return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of nodes in the graph const size_t localTiles = static_cast<size_t>(d.NLI) * d.NLJ;\n    const size_t localElems = std::max<size_t>(localTiles * TT, 1);\n    const size_t colElems = {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793142446707,"sessionID":"ses_e807c23a9ffecLzhcZkkw485d1","part":{"id":"prt_17f9e1878001wilZqD7ZOMlR5d","messageID":"msg_17f9e13000016R51GyA5xhUIXK","sessionID":"ses_e807c23a9ffecLzhcZkkw485d1","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm breaking down the kernel timing per rank — the update kernel runs about 440ms each across 4 GPUs concurrently for a 1164ms wall time, with 512 launches per rank averaging under a millisecond, while the panel kernels add roughly 92ms total on top of that.\n\nThe real gap is idle time: GPU busy time is only about 470ms per rank against a 1164ms wall clock, leaving roughly 700ms stalled on host-side synchronization — cudaStreamSynchronize calls total 1.26s across ranks, about 256 per rank. The dependency chain is the culprit: each bulk update for block K can't launch until the host finishes communication for K, which depends on panel K, which depends on the previous block's trailing columns, which depends on the bulk update two blocks back. So while bulk_{K-1} runs on the GPU, this chain of panel/comm work for block K is supposed to overlap it, but the bulk stream for block K only kicks off once comm K completes — I need to trace through the relative sizes of these dependency stages to see where the overlap breaks down.\n\nTracing the dependency chain more carefully: since bulk operations run sequentially on the same stream, each taking ~0.86ms, while comm_K requires bulk_{K-2} to finish before it can start, there's an inherent loop where the GPU can only stay one block ahead of the communication pipeline, creating the serialization bottleneck I'm seeing.\n\nI measured c (the comm latency per block) at around 4.5ms, which is way larger than x — so the issue is clear: comm isn't being hidden behind compute at all, since c needs to stay under 0.86ms. I'm breaking down what's actually inside that 4.5ms: two host syncs per block (one for the diagonal step waiting on N_{K-1}), two MPI broadcasts, and an H2D transfer all stacking up sequentially.\n\nThe real culprit is stream ordering: because N_{K-1} is enqueued after bulk_{K-2} on the same stream, the host's sync call for the diag step ends up blocking until bulk_{K-2} finishes — meaning the host can't even issue the next communication step until that earlier GPU work completes, which defeats the whole overlap strategy.\n\nThat confirms it: the host sync at the start of iteration K blocks on bulk_{K-2} finishing, which takes roughly x per block — explaining why the measured sync latency matches the bulk duration.\n\nSo the host sync on sMain actually waits for N_{K-1} which itself depends on bulk_{K-2}; since bulk_{K-1} is queued right after bulk_{K-2} on the same stream, it can't start until bulk_{K-2} completes, meaning the host wait effectively gates on that serialization point.\n\nGiven the measured total of 1164 ms over 256 iterations works out to about 4.5 ms per iteration, and the GPU kernel itself only takes 440ms of that 1164ms total, something like the broadcast communication cost (c) seems to be dominating at roughly 4.5ms per step -- suggesting MPI_Bcast on these 1MB buffers across ranks might just be inherently slow here.\n\nI should instrument the actual timing rather than guess further: add timers around the D2H transfer, the MPI_Bcast, and the H2D transfer separately in a scratch copy to pin down where the per-block latency is actually coming from. Rough estimates suggest pinned D2H/H2D at 1MB should only take ~0.17ms each and an intra-node shared-memory bcast maybe 0.1-0.3ms, so something isn't adding up and I need real measurements to find the bottleneck.\n\n","time":{"start":1793142429816,"end":1793142446636},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793142496341,"sessionID":"ses_e807c23a9ffecLzhcZkkw485d1","part":{"id":"prt_17f9eea9b001EuOx2vOi6ATw2r","messageID":"msg_17f9ee526001bCYhdGWk1ena7l","sessionID":"ses_e807c23a9ffecLzhcZkkw485d1","type":"reasoning","text":"Looking at the rank0 timing breakdown, I'm trying to pin down what's eating the 304ms panelsLaunch window — it seems to cover the MPI_Bcast of the diagonal plus the host-to-device transfer for non-owner ranks, sitting right after the 264ms diagSync wait on the prior bulk update.\n\nRechecking the marker placement, the panel launches and D2H plus sync for COL/ROW only account for ~67ms, while the real cost is the 491ms stretch covering the column/row MPI broadcasts plus H2D transfers — roughly 1.9ms per block, making that the dominant bottleneck alongside the diag bcast chain and diagSync itself.\n\nI'm wondering if OpenMPI's broadcast of a 1MB buffer across 4 shared-memory ranks is just inherently slow, maybe worth isolating that cost directly. Possible fixes include checking for CUDA-aware MPI support to bcast device buffers directly and skip the D2H/H2D round trip, or restructuring to issue a single combined bcast instead of separate column/row ones, or using MPI_Ibcast to overlap communication — though there's a structural dependency since block K's data depends on the previous panel finishing first.\n\nThe real bottleneck seems to be the critical chain itself: each block's panel computation waits on a stream sync that depends on the prior bulk update, and even though the host blocks during MPI_Bcast while the GPU keeps running the previous bulk operation, the per-block wall time still works out to roughly 4.4ms when comm (around 1.9ms) dominates over the 0.86ms bulk compute. I suspect rank skew from accumulated GPU-stream waits is inflating the bcast cost beyond what a plain 1MB broadcast should take, so the real win might come from shortening or decoupling that dependency chain rather than just overlapping communication.\n\nI'm wondering if I could reorder bulk computation to prioritize the row/col tiles needed next, splitting off a \"critical\" portion first. But really the dominant cost is communication latency — roughly 4.4ms per block from the broadcasts and syncs — so maybe combining the diagonal, column, and row exchanges into fewer messages could help, though that's tricky since different ranks need different pieces.\n\nGiven we're only hitting ~1.8x speedup on 4 GPUs, I should stop theorizing and actually measure: I'll write a quick microbenchmark timing MPI_Bcast for a 1MB buffer across 2 and 4 ranks to see if OpenMPI's broadcast implementation itself is the bottleneck.\n\n","time":{"start":1793142483611,"end":1793142496324},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Peer-to-peer GPU memcpy or CUDA IPC would avoid MPI for intra-node exchanges but add complexity, so instead I'm considering reducing and overlapping the sequential exchanges per block to cut down on the diagonal broadcast overhead.\n\nRealistically I could gain maybe 2x on comm by overlapping col/row broadcasts with MPI_Ibcast, though concurrent bandwidth contention across 4 ranks may limit this. The core problem is the diag+col+row broadcast chain (~2.2ms) is longer than the bulk compute (0.86ms) per block, so comm dominates — increasing tile size reduces block count but raises per-block comm volume, so it's a tradeoff I need to balance carefully.\n\nWorking through the math, total comm volume actually stays fixed at roughly n²*4 bytes regardless of tile size, so larger tiles mainly reduce latency count rather than total data moved — but shared-memory limits cap the tile at 64, since 96 would exceed the 48KB default smem budget.\n\nConfirming the per-rank calculation: with P=Q=2 and n=16384, comm volume works out to about 1GB per rank, and at ~1GB/s effective bandwidth that's roughly a 1-second cost, matching what I estimated earlier. So the 2D decomposition is genuinely communication-bound here, with panel broadcasts dominating the runtime.\n\nI'm wondering if switching to GPU-to-GPU peer copies (cudaMemcpyPeer or CUDA IPC handles) instead of MPI host staging could drastically cut this, since PCIe P2P bandwidth is far higher -- though setting up IPC handles across separate MPI processes adds real complexity and fragility. Before going down that path, I should check whether the 1GB/s figure is actually an artifact of MPI shared-memory (vader) contention among four processes or a VM limitation, so testing raw host memcpy bandwidth directly would clarify that.\n\nComparing pinned D2H transfer rates against two-rank versus four-rank broadcast timings, it looks like the slowdown is specific to having four ranks, likely due to contention in the shared-memory transport or a multi-level broadcast tree requiring sequential copies. Given the 2D decomposition, the receive volume per block is inherently tied to both the local panel heights, so reducing data volume isn't trivial since each rank genuinely needs the full column panel to update all its tiles -- this points toward needing a different transport mechanism rather than a smaller payload.\n\nI'm working through whether a 1D column-block decomposition would help instead, but the total communication volume turns out to be roughly the same as the 2D case since each rank still needs to receive the full pivot column. At n=16384 with four GPUs, computing the comparison between compute time (~0.44s) and communication time (~0.5s at 2GB/s) suggests the run is essentially communication-bound at this scale with host-staged MPI.\n\nGiven the time constraints, I'm weighing practical mitigations like overlapping column and row broadcasts with MPI_Ibcast, reducing host synchronization points, and reconsidering whether 4 ranks is actually optimal versus 2 or 1 rank — noting 1302ms for 2 ranks versus 1132ms for 4 versus 2090ms for 1. That single-GPU timing also hints the kernel itself may not be using the 3090's full integer throughput efficiently.\n\nThe per-thread update loop does roughly 4-5 operations (add, compare, two conditional selects) per element per k-step, plus shared memory loads, and I estimate the achieved throughput is around 2.1 TOps/s against a theoretical peak near 17.8 TIOPS for int32 — suggesting there's real room (maybe 2-3x) to improve by restructuring the kernel with larger register tiles or reducing redundant updates, which would also shift the comm-to-compute ratio favorably.\n\nI'm weighing whether it's worth trying to cut the per-element op count further (e.g. using IMNMX for the min and a single select for the path update) versus accepting that single-GPU is close to ALU-bound and the real gap is in communication overlap across 4 GPUs — leaning toward trying an overlapping MPI_Ibcast approach instead of squeezing more kernel efficiency.\n\nMaybe issuing them together with Waitall lets concurrency hide the latency. I should try a quick microbench with two separate communicators for rows and cols, and test MPI_Bcast with different mca tuning options to see if that changes the picture.\n\nGiven the time invested, I think a reasonable stopping point is one more quick experiment: swap the row and column MPI_Bcast calls for an MPI_Ibcast pair with Waitall in the profiling copy, including the diagonal case.
